narrative:
The model estimates a 52% chance that you will leave your job, which is just over the threshold for predicting departure. Because of this, the company has decided to deny your promotion.

The decision was driven primarily by three key factors in your profile. Most influential was that you have not received any other job offers while working here. Among employees the model expects to stay, 77% also report no external opportunities, yet this absence still pulled the prediction toward leaving, likely signaling limited external pull that can sometimes correlate with eventual departure in this dataset.

The second most important factor was your 6-10 years in your current role. This is longer than most employees the model predicts will stay (over half have only 1-5 years here), and it pushed the prediction toward you leaving. The model appears to associate mid-length tenure in one organization with higher turnover risk.

Your overall career experience of 6-10 years worked in the opposite direction, modestly encouraging a prediction that you would stay. This is actually more experience than half the employees predicted to remain, who mostly fall in the 1-5 year range.

Taken together, the lack of outside offers and your current tenure outweighed your broader experience, tipping the model just past 50%. The organization should discuss your career goals with you directly and explore whether additional internal opportunities or support could strengthen your commitment. You may also want to reflect on what would make staying feel more rewarding long-term. (248 words)
